content:
Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan conceded his loss Tuesday to Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola an entire week after major networks had already declared him the loser — and with a social media post that appears to have been published from Florida.

“As we head into Thanksgiving, Julie and I are filled with gratitude,” Sullivan wrote Tuesday on X. “Serving Alaska in the United States Senate for the past 12 years has been the honor of a lifetime, and I thank all Alaskans for that opportunity.”

He continued, “As I’ve always said I would, and out of respect for the people of Alaska and our democratic process, I accept the results certified by the Division of Elections. Alaskans deserve confidence in the integrity of their elections.”

Sullivan appeared to share the post at 1:50 p.m. from Upper Grand Lagoon, Florida, according to location data captured in a screenshot by the Politics & Poll Tracker account on X. The post was updated at 2:02 p.m. — with the location changed to Anchorage, Alaska.

Sullivan, whom President Donald Trump endorsed and who joined numerous other Republicans who lost to Democrats in the midterms, was promptly roasted on social media. One X user wrote, “Was Sen Dan Sullivan at Mar a Lago?”

Some social media users slammed Sullivan for omitting any mention of Peltola in his post, and despite his finally conceding the race, Sullivan also seemed to revive Trump’s longstanding suggestion that it was hobbled by Democratic “voter fraud.”

Sullivan wrote, “I trust that the ongoing federal and state investigations will provide answers to the questions that remain,” in an apparent reference to the fact that he was not only running against Peltola — but against another candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan.

The New York Times reported last month that Peltola’s campaign was involved in a scheme to recruit Daniel J. Sullivan into the race. Trump’s DOJ then argued that his candidacy would mislead people hoping to vote for the incumbent Republican, threatening to block the election results if Peltola won.

Peltola’s campaign and Daniel J. Sullivan himself denied the allegations — and a sample of Alaska’s midterms ballot clearly distinguished the two Dan Sullivans.

Daniel J. Sullivan ultimately received fewer than 5,000 votes — not enough to affect the results. Peltola earned 50.1% of the vote (144,583 votes), and the GOP incumbent earned 45.8% (132,022 votes). The Trump administration formally gave up last week on its legal effort to block the results.

Sullivan, meanwhile, was roasted on social media for thanking Alaskans in a concession post published from the Sunshine State.
